title: Intelligent maintenance slices for throughput isolation during node lifecycle operations
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Problem: Rolling node maintenance (OS/kernel patches, driver upgrades, eviction) causes transient throughput degradation on Dedicated fleets. Current drains are time-based and treat capacity as homogeneous, which leads to bursts of token latency or short-lived throughput cliffs for customers with tight SLOs. Goal: implement a maintenance orchestration primitive that breaks a maintenance window into smaller "slices" and coordinates throughput reservations and routing so that per-customer throughput guarantees and latency SLOs are preserved during node lifecycle events.

Scope: implement controller logic and API for scheduling maintenance slices, changes to the autoscaler to honor slice reservations, runtime hooks for soft-drain versus hard-drain, observability metrics and dashboards, and a rollout plan for Dedicated fleets. This ticket focuses on the orchestration and routing/reservation layer; runtime invocation and kernel-level migration will be separate follow-ups.

Non-goals: full kernel live-migration, customer-visible UI in Console (backend API only for now), reworking quota system (only temporarily reserve existing quota buckets).

Design summary:
- Maintenance slices: split a maintenance window (e.g., 2 hours) into N small slices (e.g., 12x10min). Each slice has a reservation plan that declares throughput budget reductions per-route/model (absolute tokens/sec or relative percent) and a preferred drain mode (soft-prefetch, degrade-to-variant, final-evict).
- Reservation planner: computes per-slice budgets based on historical traffic, active reservations, and contract-level throughput guarantees. Planner emits reservations expressed as token-per-second budgets for the autoscaler and routing layer.
- Route-aware steering: routing layer applies temporary capacity reservations by steering lower-priority traffic to fallback variants or to different regions to maintain reserved throughput for high-SLA tenants.
- Incremental drain modes: soft-drain reduces new connection acceptance and migrates cached prefixes; hard-drain only used during final slice if migration fails.
- Autoscaler integration: autoscaler treats reservations as absolute floor capacity to maintain during slices; it will prevent scale-downs that would violate active reservations and will coordinate burst capacity when a slice begins.
- Observability: new metrics (slice_id, reserved_tps, actual_tps, slice_health, migration_failures) and dashboard templates for on-call and SRE.

Tradeoffs and constraints:
- Conservatism vs cost: conservative reservations increase cost for the maintenance window; we will prefer percentile-based planning (p95 traffic) with optional slack.
- Complexity vs predictability: route-aware steering increases routing decisions; we limit scope to prioritized routes (top 50 by spend) in rollout.
- Backward compatibility: system falls back to current global drain when planner disabled.

Rollout plan:
1) API + planner prototype (backend, no autoscaler enforcement) - internal testing (2 weeks).
2) Autoscaler acceptance of reservation signals and dry-run enforcement (3 weeks).
3) Route steering for prioritized routes + observability (2 weeks).
4) Canary maintenance on single dedicated fleet (1 week) + verify SLOs.
5) Gradual ramp to 25% of fleets, then 100% with opt-in flag.

Success metrics: preserved per-tenant throughput within SLA thresholds during maintenance windows (>99% of checks), reduced 95th-percentile latency spikes during maintenance by >= 60%, and no more than 10% additional cost during windows when using default planner settings.
acceptance_criteria: Planner can slice a maintenance window and emit per-slice reservation plans (JSON) with reserved_tps per route.
Autoscaler accepts reservation signals and will not scale below reserved capacity in dry-run mode.
Routing layer applies steering for prioritized routes and records slice metrics (reserved_tps, actual_tps, slice_health).
Canary maintenance run preserves high-SLA tenant throughput within configured thresholds for at least 95% of slices.
Dashboards show slice-level metrics and alerts trigger when slice_health < 0.9 or migration_failures spike.
Fallback to legacy global drain when planner is disabled without impacting runtime stability.
steps: Write design doc and API contract (Confluence: /d/dedicated/maintenance-slices).
Implement planner prototype that ingests historical traffic and outputs slice reservations.
Add reservation signal API to autoscaler and implement dry-run enforcement mode.
Extend routing layer to accept per-slice steering directives for prioritized routes.
Add telemetry: slice_id, reserved_tps, actual_tps, slice_health, migration_failures.
Run canary maintenance on non-critical dedicated fleet and measure success metrics.
Iterate planner heuristics to reduce cost while meeting SLOs; prepare rollout runbook.
